newsitem.title: USA: Mercury says gets loan waivers extension.
newsitem.headline: Mercury says gets loan waivers extension.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Tuesday that BankAmerica Corp's Bank of America had extended to March 14 the deadline for Mercury to obtain a continuation of waivers for its $50 million short-term credit facility. The previous deadline was March 10.
Waivers are required from certain lenders whose loan agreements restrict the company's ability to pledge its assets as collateral, Mercury said.
"Mercury is in discussions with its lenders with respect to terms for permitting the waivers to continue," the company said.
Bank of America "also indicated that it is prepared to extend the maturity of the loan to June 10, 1997, if the waivers permit," said Mercury, a sub-prime auto lender.

Mercury received the $50 million in short-term financing from Bank of America a month ago. The financing is being used to meet daily operating expenses and interest payments as Mercury confronts numerous difficulties.

The company faces a federal investigation, several shareholder lawsuits, restatement of financial results due to accounting irregularities, and a loss of more than $2 billion in market capitalization after a plunge in its stock price.
